breakpoints.code: HashTable *values = php_fgetcsv(NULL, delim, enc, esc, ZSTR_LEN(str), ZSTR_VAL(str));
breakpoints.note: First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled PHP string and CSV control characters into vulnerability-relevant parser state. The staged script reaches `str_getcsv("\xFF", "", "\xFF", "\x00")`, so this call forwards the exact one-byte data buffer, enclosure byte `0xFF`, and escape byte `0x00` into `php_fgetcsv`.

Root cause fixed by the patch. In the `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup, vulnerable code only retreats `bptr` when parsing has advanced past `limit`; it omits the added `if (hunk_begin == bptr) --hunk_begin;` obligation, so the witness can leave `hunk_begin > bptr` and make the later copy length negative.
